clue.text: Singer travelling on recent tour

indicators.note: things travelling move about, so the letters of these three words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A vocalist is on the road, having just gone on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' looks like part of the touring story but signals the anagram of ON RECENT TOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A countertenor is a male singer whose voice sits in the alto range, so he is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Hard-hearted relative drops in, overwhelming everyone

indicators.note: overwhelming means the remaining letters surround and swamp the word for everyone
drops means the word in is let fall from the relative's name

parts.note: a cousin is a relative
everyone means all

explanation.surface: An unfeeling family member drops by and crushes the whole household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' reads as 'pays a visit', but 'drops' tells you to remove 'in' from the relative, and 'overwhelming' wraps what is left round the word for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous and hard-hearted are synonyms, both describing someone without sympathy for others.

clue.text: Planning ahead, couple take week off

parts.note: to be one up is to be ahead, so ahead gives up

indicators.note: take off means the letter for week is removed from the word for a couple
off completes take off, the letter for week leaving the word for a couple

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: Two people plan in advance and book a week's holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'take ... off' is split around 'week'. 'Planning' fits as in 'what are you up to?'
explanation.definitionFit: To be up to something is to be planning or plotting it, as in asking what someone is up to.

clue.text: Most small pixels frequently hidden by colour

indicators.note: hidden by means the picked letters are tucked inside the word for colour

parts.note: a tint is a colour

indicators.note: frequently means taking letters at regular intervals, here every other letter of pixels

explanation.surface: The tiniest dots on a screen often vanish beneath a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frequently' picks I, E and S from pixels; 'hidden by' puts them inside TINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiniest is the superlative of tiny, meaning smallest, so it matches the phrase most small.

clue.text: Book about British accountant bored with the City

parts.note: re is Latin for about, as in letters

indicators.note: bored with means the other letters are drilled into, holding the City's code inside

parts.note: CA is chartered accountant
EC is the postcode district of the City of London

explanation.surface: A volume about a British accountant who is bored with working in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored with' reads as weary of, but means drilled into. The City is London's financial district, whose postcode is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is the novel by Daphne du Maurier, a book title.

clue.text: Earthy tone of European vintage

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or vintage of wine

explanation.surface: A natural shade drawn from an old European wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale beige-brown colour of unbleached linen, an earthy shade.

clue.text: Driving out or in got us confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of these three words are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: We got muddled over whether we were driving out or in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out or in' looks like a pair of options, but 'Driving out' is the definition and 'in' starts the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting is expelling someone, which is driving them out of a place or position.

clue.text: Running advance press, featuring current game

indicators.note: featuring means the rearranged letters include the symbol for current within them
running means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs an advance story about the latest game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' rearranges ADVANCE PRESS to SPACENVADERS, and 'featuring' slips I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Space Invaders is a classic 1978 arcade video game, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: A teacher can't initially make out where pupils come from

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged
initially means just the first letter of make is used

explanation.surface: A teacher just cannot make out where the children in the class come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make out' looks like a phrase, but 'initially' acts on 'make' alone and 'out' is the anagram signal for the teacher's letters; the A stays put at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's catchment area is the district its pupils are drawn from, so it is where they come from.

clue.text: Cycle group exercise with crowd round noon

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school
a lot is a crowd or group
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cycling club exercises with a crowd at around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The peloton is the main bunch of riders in a road cycling race, a group of cyclists.

clue.text: Rail is sited centrally alongside a drinks dispenser

parts.note: a bar is a rail

indicators.note: centrally means only the central letter of sited is used

explanation.surface: A rail is placed in the middle beside a vending machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks dispenser' suggests a machine, but it is a person serving coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes and serves coffee in a café, so they dispense drinks.

clue.text: Sweet treat that is removed in bits from selection?

indicators.note: removed in bits means the two letters come out separately, not side by side, from the selection word

parts.note: a choice is a selection
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sweet is picked bit by bit out of a selection box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bits' tells you the I and the E are removed from separate places in CHOICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Choc is informal British for a chocolate, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Make fine cut

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
to etch is to cut a design into a surface

explanation.surface: An instruction to produce a precise incision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like an instruction but is the definition: an item fetches or makes a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetch a sum, as at auction, is to make or bring in that amount of money.

clue.text: Police officer starts to scrutinise criminal's record

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A detective begins to examine a lawbreaker's criminal record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a police file but is a gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the vinyl kind played on a turntable.

clue.text: Sailors tackling environment-related survey

indicators.note: tackling means the sailors take hold of and wrap round the environmental prefix

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
eco is the prefix for things related to the environment

explanation.surface: Naval crews take on an ecological study.
explanation.definitionFit: Recon, short for reconnaissance, is a survey of ground or enemy positions.

clue.text: Corporation with a good flipping range

indicators.note: flipping means the combined letters are flipped over and read backwards

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A company with a decent range of products, flipping marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but it is the old jokey word for a fat belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the whole range or scope of something, as in running the gamut.

clue.text: Vet wearing glasses trimmed cat's tail

parts.note: to be in something is to be wearing it

indicators.note: trimmed means the glasses word loses its final letter

parts.note: specs are glasses

indicators.note: tail means just the last letter of the word cat, the 's being a possessive link

explanation.surface: A vet in spectacles clips a cat's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' is a verb here, not the animal doctor the surface suggests; 'trimmed' cuts the last letter from SPECS.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to check or examine it carefully, the same as to inspect it.

clue.text: Publication hit back following a merger

indicators.note: following means the reversed letters come after the word a
back means the publication and hit words are read backwards

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication
to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A magazine hit back after a corporate merger.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or mixture, the product of a merger of different elements.

clue.text: Thick people of rank dismissing books

indicators.note: dismissing means the books are sent out of the word for the nobles

parts.note: viscounts are noblemen, people of rank
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Stupid aristocrats reject reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' suggests stupid; it means sticky in consistency.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscous liquid is thick and slow-flowing, like syrup.

clue.text: Influential artist embodied by Spall occasionally

indicators.note: embodied by means the artist sits inside the picked letters
occasionally means only some letters of Spall are used, every other one

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: An artist of influence is portrayed by the actor Timothy Spall now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes S, A and L from Spall; EMIN goes inside. Timothy Spall is a British actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work is highly influential, shaping later developments.

clue.text: Island located in such an extraordinary part of China

indicators.note: located in means the island letter is placed within the rearranged letters
extraordinary means the letters of such an are made unusual by rearrangement

explanation.surface: An island found in such a remarkable region of China.
explanation.definitionFit: Sichuan is a province in south-west China, so it is a part of that country.

clue.text: Gourmand's grand time in town

definitions.note: read as gourmand is, so the definition is a gourmand

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: in means the time letter is put inside the town's name

parts.note: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire, England

explanation.surface: A food lover has a great time in town.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay. LUTON is an English town north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand loves food and eats a great deal, so he is essentially a glutton.

clue.text: I endlessly go back, up and around to get blanket

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, in reverse
endlessly means the last letter is lost from the word for going back

parts.note: to renege is to go back on a promise
C is circa, around

explanation.surface: I keep turning back and round to fetch a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blanket' looks like a noun but is the adjective, as in a blanket ban; 'up' reverses I + RENEG to GENERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket as an adjective means covering everything, which is what generic means: applying to a whole class.

clue.text: Climbing frame very badly erected inside

indicators.note: inside means the turned letters go within the French word

parts.note: tres is French for very

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means set upright, so the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A climbing frame is put up very badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing frame' suggests a children's playground, but it is a frame for climbing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice for climbing plants to grow up, a frame for climbers.

clue.text: Certain rule accepted by party for trial

indicators.note: accepted by means the rule is taken inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
an em rule is a kind of dash in printing, so one certain rule is em

explanation.surface: A firm regulation is adopted by a political party on a trial basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rule' looks like a law, but an em rule is a printer's long dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a demonstration or trial run of a product or recording.

clue.text: Going up without using a track

indicators.note: without using means the word a is left out of the climbing word

parts.note: an ascent is a going up

explanation.surface: Climbing without the aid of a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track' looks like a path but is the trail an animal leaves for hounds to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is the trail of smell an animal leaves, which hunters follow as a track.

clue.text: Unknown projected delivery date for letter from abroad

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown
ETA is the estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: No date is given for when an overseas letter will arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter from abroad' suggests post, but means a letter of a foreign alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeta is the sixth letter of the Greek alphabet, a letter from a foreign script.

clue.text: Brilliant finish to University Challenge

parts.note: def is slang for excellent or brilliant

indicators.note: finish to means the closing letter of University

explanation.surface: A superb ending to the TV quiz University Challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: University Challenge is a long-running British TV quiz for university teams.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy someone is to challenge or resist them openly.

clue.text: No more eggs, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word for eggs is said and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: ova are eggs

explanation.surface: We seem to have run out of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means finished, so when something is over there is no more of it.

clue.text: Fiddled around, capturing electronic piece of music

indicators.note: capturing means the rearranged letters hold the electronic letter inside
fiddled means the letters of around are tampered with and rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone played the fiddle around a recording of an electronic track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddled' suggests a violin, fitting the music theme, but signals the anagram of AROUND, RONDAU, with E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a medieval French song form with a refrain, a piece of music.

clue.text: Twist arm, almost

indicators.note: almost means the weapon word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a revolver is a firearm, an arm

explanation.surface: An arm being nearly twisted, as in a playground struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb to twist, but is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve is to turn round, a synonym of twist in the sense of rotate.

clue.text: Profitable comedians entertaining large clubs, perhaps

indicators.note: entertaining means the profitable word plays host to the letter for large inside it

parts.note: a paying venture is profitable
cards are amusing people, comedians

explanation.surface: Well-paid comics perform at big nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' tells you PAYING holds L inside it; 'clubs' is a card suit, not a nightspot.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the four suits in a pack, so it is an example of playing cards.
